claim: The entry of calcium into mitochondria is central to metabolism, inter-organelle communication, and cell life/death decisions.
source: The entry of calcium into mitochondria is central to metabolism, inter-organelle communication, and cell life/death decisions.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific understanding about mitochondrial calcium function.

claim: Long-sought transporters involved in mitochondrial calcium influx and efflux have recently been identified.
source: Long-sought transporters involved in mitochondrial calcium influx and efflux have recently been identified.
evidence: This refers to recent scientific discoveries in the field, supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Amorphous solid granules containing calcium and phosphorus were pervasive in the mitochondrial matrices of a variety of mammalian cell types.
source: Amorphous solid granules containing calcium and phosphorus were pervasive in the mitochondrial matrices of a variety of mammalian cell types.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by CSTET imaging data and EDX spectroscopy shown in the figures.

claim: Analysis based on quantitative electron scattering revealed that these repositories are equivalent to molar concentrations of dissolved ions.
source: Analysis based on quantitative electron scattering revealed that these repositories are equivalent to molar concentrations of dissolved ions.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis presented in Tables 1-3 and the methods section.

claim: Calcium buffering in the mitochondrial matrix in live cells occurs by phase separation.
source: These results demonstrate conclusively that calcium buffering in the mitochondrial matrix in live cells occurs by phase separation, and that solid-phase stores provide a major ion reservoir that can be mobilized for bioenergetics and signaling.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the observation of solid granules in vitrified cells.

claim: Solid-phase stores provide a major ion reservoir that can be mobilized for bioenergetics and signaling.
source: These results demonstrate conclusively that calcium buffering in the mitochondrial matrix in live cells occurs by phase separation, and that solid-phase stores provide a major ion reservoir that can be mobilized for bioenergetics and signaling.
evidence: This is inferred from the quantitative analysis showing molar concentrations and the observation that granules disappear upon FCCP treatment.

claim: The proton gradient in mitochondria allows for oxidative phosphorylation in the production of ATP.
source: A widely known example is the proton gradient in mitochondria, which allows for oxidative phosphorylation in the production of ATP (Saraste, 1999).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Calcium ions affect mitochondrial physiology by regulating respiratory chain complexes, tricarboxylic acid cycle proteins, and metabolite transporters.
source: Calcium ions affect mitochondrial physiology by regulating respiratory chain complexes, tricarboxylic acid cycle proteins, and metabolite transporters (Glancy and Balaban, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Substantial potential energy is stored in the calcium gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane.
source: Furthermore, substantial potential energy is stored in the calcium gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane (Glancy and Balaban, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Calcium uptake by mitochondria influences cellular calcium signaling.
source: Calcium uptake by mitochondria also influences cellular calcium signaling (Rizzuto et al., 2012) and, in excess, can trigger apoptotic cell death (Giorgi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Excess calcium uptake by mitochondria can trigger apoptotic cell death.
source: Calcium uptake by mitochondria also influences cellular calcium signaling (Rizzuto et al., 2012) and, in excess, can trigger apoptotic cell death (Giorgi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Fluorescent indicators inevitably perturb the soluble ion pool.
source: Although fluorescent indicators are widely used in the study of mitochondrial calcium dynamics (Pendin et al., 2015), these sensors inevitably perturb the soluble ion pool.
evidence: This is a known limitation of fluorescent indicators, supported by the observation that JC-1 damaged mitochondrial ultrastructure in this study.

claim: Fluorescent indicators are blind to solid-phase stores or tightly bound species.
source: Moreover, they are blind to solid-phase stores or tightly bound species.
evidence: This is a known limitation of fluorescent calcium indicators.

claim: Ions and other unfixed contents are likely to be flushed from the organelle during sample preparation for conventional TEM.
source: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) of metal-stained thin cell sections has for decades provided details on mitochondrial morphology and interactions (Palade, 1953; Lee et al., 2016), but ions and other unfixed contents are likely to be flushed from the organelle during sample preparation.
evidence: This is inferred from the nature of conventional TEM sample preparation methods.

claim: CSTET provides deep views into cells up to >1 μm.
source: We note that CSTET is well suited to provide deep views (up to >1 μm) into cells (Rez et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and demonstrated by the tomograms collected in this study.

claim: Conventional cryo-TEM tomography is restricted to thin cell regions (preferably less than 300 nm).
source: For comparison, conventional cryo-TEM tomography is restricted to thin cell regions (preferably less than 300 nm) (Villa et al., 2013) or requires technically challenging processing of thicker regions by cryo-microtomy (Ladinsky et al., 2006) or focused-ion beam milling (Marko et al., 2007; Mahamid et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Conventional metal-stained thin sections of fixed cells are approximately 70-nm thick.
source: Conventional metal-stained thin sections of fixed cells (Figure 1A) are approximately 70-nm thick and unavoidably display staining artifacts.
evidence: This is a known characteristic of conventional TEM sample preparation.

claim: Conventional metal-stained thin sections unavoidably display staining artifacts.
source: Conventional metal-stained thin sections of fixed cells (Figure 1A) are approximately 70-nm thick and unavoidably display staining artifacts.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 1A and is a known limitation of the technique.

claim: ER is juxtaposed to a mitochondrial constriction with numerous microtubules crossing the junction at acute angles and wrapping around the mitochondria with a gentle twist.
source: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is seen juxtaposed to a mitochondrial constriction with numerous microtubules crossing the junction at acute angles and wrapping around the mitochondria with a gentle twist (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly observed in the CSTET reconstruction shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Large (~500 nm diameter) vesicles are seen budding from near the mitochondrial junction.
source: In addition, large (~500 nm diameter) vesicles are seen in their entirety budding from near the junction, and lipid droplets are present in the vicinity (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This is directly observed in the CSTET reconstruction shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: Dense granules were consistently observed within mitochondria in a variety of mammalian cell types.
source: In normative intracellular contexts such as those described above, we consistently observed dense granules within mitochondria in a variety of mammalian cell types (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplements 1–2, and Videos 1–9).
evidence: This is demonstrated across multiple figures and cell types in the study.

claim: Granules are dispersed between flat lamellar cristae and adjacent to well-formed junctions between cristae and the inner mitochondrial membrane.
source: Figure 1D shows granules dispersed between flat lamellar cristae and adjacent to well-formed junctions between cristae and the inner mitochondrial membrane.
evidence: This is directly observed in Figure 1D.

claim: The presence of granules did not require mitochondrial proximity to the ER.
source: The presence of granules did not require mitochondrial proximity to the ER, nor did granule appearance correlate with mitochondrial shape (round or elongated) (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is observed across multiple mitochondria in different cellular contexts.

claim: Granule appearance did not correlate with mitochondrial shape (round or elongated).
source: The presence of granules did not require mitochondrial proximity to the ER, nor did granule appearance correlate with mitochondrial shape (round or elongated) (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 1E showing both spherical and elongated mitochondria with similar granule distributions.

claim: Granule diameters ranged from about 20 to 100 nm, varying with cell type.
source: Granule diameters ranged from about 20 to 100 nm, varying with cell type.
evidence: This is measured from the CSTET data across different cell types.

claim: No granules were seen in fully constricted fission tubules.
source: As expected, no granules were seen in fully constricted fission tubules, which had a minimum diameter of approximately 15 nm and from which matrix was excluded.
evidence: This is observed in the CSTET data.

claim: Fully constricted fission tubules had a minimum diameter of approximately 15 nm.
source: As expected, no granules were seen in fully constricted fission tubules, which had a minimum diameter of approximately 15 nm and from which matrix was excluded.
evidence: This is measured from the CSTET data.

claim: Matrix was excluded from fully constricted fission tubules.
source: As expected, no granules were seen in fully constricted fission tubules, which had a minimum diameter of approximately 15 nm and from which matrix was excluded.
evidence: This is observed in the CSTET data.

claim: Granules were seen in mitochondria both near the cell periphery and adjacent to the nucleus.
source: Granules were seen in mitochondria both near the cell periphery (Figure 1B) and adjacent to the nucleus (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figures 1B and 1F.

claim: Dense spots of similar size have appeared without description or discussion in published cryo-TEM images.
source: We note that dense spots of similar size have appeared without description or discussion in published cryo-TEM images (Faas et al., 2012; Woodward et al., 2015), supporting the notion that granules are widely found in mammalian mitochondria.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior published images.

claim: Granules are widely found in mammalian mitochondria.
source: We note that dense spots of similar size have appeared without description or discussion in published cryo-TEM images (Faas et al., 2012; Woodward et al., 2015), supporting the notion that granules are widely found in mammalian mitochondria.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of granules in multiple cell types in this study and their appearance in prior published images.

claim: EDX spectroscopy gave signals for both calcium and phosphorus from granule-rich mitochondria but not from adjacent cytosolic regions.
source: Energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopy gave signals for both calcium and phosphorus from granule-rich mitochondria but not from adjacent cytosolic regions (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2A showing EDX spectra.

claim: Diffraction effects (blinking in the bright field) were not observed during the tilt series acquisitions for tomography, indicating that the granules were not crystalline.
source: Diffraction effects (blinking in the bright field) were not observed during the tilt series acquisitions for tomography, indicating that the granules were not crystalline.
evidence: This is an observation from the CSTET data collection and an inference about granule structure.

claim: Mitochondrial matrix granules in intact cells are composed of amorphous calcium phosphate.
source: We conclude that mitochondrial matrix granules in intact cells are composed of amorphous calcium phosphate, as was surmised (Lehninger, 1970; Chalmers and Nicholls, 2003) but never directly demonstrated in samples not subjected to fixation or dehydration.
evidence: This is concluded from EDX data showing calcium and phosphorus and the absence of diffraction effects indicating amorphous structure.

claim: Amorphous calcium phosphate composition of mitochondrial granules was surmised but never directly demonstrated in samples not subjected to fixation or dehydration.
source: We conclude that mitochondrial matrix granules in intact cells are composed of amorphous calcium phosphate, as was surmised (Lehninger, 1970; Chalmers and Nicholls, 2003) but never directly demonstrated in samples not subjected to fixation or dehydration.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work that proposed this composition.

claim: Strong high-angle scattering by mitochondrial granules is consistent with a composition biased toward elements heavier than the oxygen dominating the surrounding aqueous medium.
source: Strong high-angle scattering by mitochondrial granules (i.e. black appearance in the BF image and white in the DF) (Figure 2C) is consistent with a composition biased toward elements heavier than the oxygen dominating the surrounding aqueous medium.
evidence: This is inferred from the scattering properties observed in BF and DF images.

claim: Ribosomes appear dark in the BF and are moderately bright in the DF due to their density and content of relatively heavy elements, including phosphorus.
source: Ribosomes (Figure 2D) also appear dark in the BF and are moderately bright in the DF due to their density and content of relatively heavy elements, including phosphorus.
evidence: This is observed in Figure 2D and explained by the known composition of ribosomes.

claim: Lipid droplets are characteristically dark in both the BF and the DF images due to their dense composition of the light element carbon.
source: For comparison, lipid droplets (Figure 2E) are characteristically dark in both the BF and the DF images due to their dense composition of the light element carbon.
evidence: This is observed in Figure 2E and explained by the known composition of lipid droplets.

claim: Mitochondrial matrices are darker in the BF than the surrounding cytosol, suggesting the presence of dissolved heavy ions.
source: In addition to containing granules, mitochondrial matrices are darker in the BF than the surrounding cytosol (Figures 1 and 2), suggesting the presence of dissolved heavy ions.
evidence: This is observed in the CSTET data and interpreted as indicating dissolved ions.

claim: The concentration of matrix calcium ions would reach a maximum of only 100 mM at electrochemical equilibrium.
source: This limitation was not surprising, considering that the concentration of matrix calcium ions would reach a maximum of only 100 mM at electrochemical equilibrium, and actual steady-state levels are considerably lower (Pozzan et al., 2000), whereas the concentrations of ions in solid deposits are much higher, as shown below.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Actual steady-state levels of matrix calcium are considerably lower than the electrochemical equilibrium maximum.
source: This limitation was not surprising, considering that the concentration of matrix calcium ions would reach a maximum of only 100 mM at electrochemical equilibrium, and actual steady-state levels are considerably lower (Pozzan et al., 2000), whereas the concentrations of ions in solid deposits are much higher, as shown below.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The concentrations of ions in solid deposits are much higher than dissolved matrix calcium.
source: This limitation was not surprising, considering that the concentration of matrix calcium ions would reach a maximum of only 100 mM at electrochemical equilibrium, and actual steady-state levels are considerably lower (Pozzan et al., 2000), whereas the concentrations of ions in solid deposits are much higher, as shown below.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the quantitative analysis in Tables 1-3.

claim: Individual matrix granules display substantial heterogeneity of intensities in 3D.
source: The substantial heterogeneity of intensities observed in 3D within individual matrix granules (Figure 2F) is consistent with a composition of 'micro-packets' of solid calcium phosphate (Lehninger, 1970).
evidence: This is observed in Figure 2F.

claim: The heterogeneity of intensities within granules is consistent with a composition of 'micro-packets' of solid calcium phosphate.
source: The substantial heterogeneity of intensities observed in 3D within individual matrix granules (Figure 2F) is consistent with a composition of 'micro-packets' of solid calcium phosphate (Lehninger, 1970).
evidence: This is inferred from the observed heterogeneity and supported by a citation.

claim: Mitochondrial and synthetic amorphous calcium phosphate particles both display granularity and appear to be composed of smaller subparticles of about 4 nm in diameter.
source: Mitochondrial and synthetic particles both display granularity and appear to be composed of smaller subparticles of about 4 nm in diameter (Figure 2H,I).
evidence: This is observed in Figure 2H,I comparing mitochondrial and synthetic particles.

claim: The general features and appearance of the mitochondrial and synthetic granules are similar.
source: The general features and appearance of the mitochondrial and synthetic granules are similar, as are the EDX spectra (Figure 2A,J).
evidence: This is observed by comparing Figures 2H,I and the EDX spectra in Figures 2A,J.

claim: The EDX spectra of mitochondrial and synthetic amorphous calcium phosphate granules are similar.
source: The general features and appearance of the mitochondrial and synthetic granules are similar, as are the EDX spectra (Figure 2A,J).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figures 2A and 2J.

claim: The most strongly scattering regions of the matrix granules were estimated to be 34–48% the density of crystalline tricalcium phosphate (TCP).
source: The most strongly scattering regions of the matrix granules in CSTET experiments were estimated to be 34–48% the density of crystalline tricalcium phosphate (TCP) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1; Tables 1–3).
evidence: This is calculated from quantitative analysis of voxel intensities in CSTET reconstructions.

claim: Granules occupied up to 20% of mitochondrial volumes of mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs).
source: Granules occupied up to 20% of mitochondrial volumes of mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is measured from segmentation of MEF mitochondria.

claim: If solubilized within the matrix volume, granule material would correspond to molar calcium and phosphate concentrations.
source: If solubilized within the matrix volume, granule material would correspond to molar calcium and phosphate concentrations, showing that mitochondria in living cells sequester substantial ion reserves in solid form.
evidence: This is calculated from the density and volume fraction measurements.

claim: Mitochondria in living cells sequester substantial ion reserves in solid form.
source: If solubilized within the matrix volume, granule material would correspond to molar calcium and phosphate concentrations, showing that mitochondria in living cells sequester substantial ion reserves in solid form.
evidence: This is concluded from the quantitative analysis of granule density and volume.

claim: After treatment with doxorubicin, CSTET revealed dramatically increased organelle fragmentation and formation of autophagosomes/autolysosomes.
source: After treatment of human primary embryonic lung fibroblasts with the chemotherapeutic agent doxorubicin, CSTET revealed dramatically increased organelle fragmentation and formation of autophagosomes/autolysosomes (Figure 3A), as well as instances of mitochondrial aggregation (Figure 3B), reported to occur in early-stage apoptosis (Haga et al., 2003).
evidence: This is observed in Figure 3A of doxorubicin-treated cells.

claim: Doxorubicin treatment resulted in instances of mitochondrial aggregation, reported to occur in early-stage apoptosis.
source: After treatment of human primary embryonic lung fibroblasts with the chemotherapeutic agent doxorubicin, CSTET revealed dramatically increased organelle fragmentation and formation of autophagosomes/autolysosomes (Figure 3A), as well as instances of mitochondrial aggregation (Figure 3B), reported to occur in early-stage apoptosis (Haga et al., 2003).
evidence: This is observed in Figure 3B and supported by a citation.

claim: Matrix granules in doxorubicin-treated cells were generally similar to those in mitochondria of untreated cells.
source: Matrix granules in doxorubicin-treated cells (Figure 3A,B) were generally similar to those in mitochondria of untreated cells (Figure 1B,D,E).
evidence: This is observed by comparing figures of treated and untreated cells.

claim: Two mitochondria only 700 nm apart but in distinct microenvironments showed striking differences in granule size and density.
source: Interestingly, we visualized in a doxorubicin-treated cell two mitochondria only 700 nm apart but in distinct microenvironments: one associated with cytoskeletal elements in the cytosol and the other sequestered with highly fragmented ER remnants, as if in the process of being decommissioned. Notably, these two mitochondria showed striking differences in granule size and density (Figure 3C), likely reflecting their distinct energetic states and diverging fates.
evidence: This is observed in Figure 3C.

claim: The differences in granule size and density between nearby mitochondria likely reflect their distinct energetic states and diverging fates.
source: Notably, these two mitochondria showed striking differences in granule size and density (Figure 3C), likely reflecting their distinct energetic states and diverging fates.
evidence: This is inferred from the observed differences in granule characteristics and the distinct cellular contexts of the two mitochondria.

claim: Both the large and small granules in doxorubicin-treated cells consisted of amorphous material.
source: Both the large and small granules consisted of amorphous material.
evidence: This is inferred from the absence of diffraction effects.

claim: In a cell region showing particularly severe damage and organelle degradation, structures that may have been fragmented mitochondria contained dense clusters of fibers or crystalline needles.
source: In contrast, in a different cell region showing particularly severe damage and organelle degradation, structures that may have been fragmented mitochondria contained dense clusters of fibers or crystalline needles (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is observed in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Embryonic fibroblasts from knockout mice lacking the mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU) showed deposits indistinguishable from control cells and containing calcium and phosphorus.
source: Embryonic fibroblasts from knockout mice lacking the mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU) (Pan et al., 2013) showed deposits indistinguishable from control cells and containing calcium and phosphorus as demonstrated by EDX analysis (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), supporting the existence of other mechanisms for calcium entry (Elustondo et al., 2017).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The presence of calcium phosphate granules in MCU knockout cells supports the existence of other mechanisms for calcium entry.
source: Embryonic fibroblasts from knockout mice lacking the mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU) (Pan et al., 2013) showed deposits indistinguishable from control cells and containing calcium and phosphorus as demonstrated by EDX analysis (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), supporting the existence of other mechanisms for calcium entry (Elustondo et al., 2017).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of granules in MCU knockout cells and supported by a citation.

claim: Calcium uptake depends on the mitochondrial membrane potential.
source: Calcium uptake depends on the mitochondrial membrane potential (Szabadkai and Duchen, 2008), and the dye JC-1, commonly used as a membrane potential reporter, enabled visualization of mitochondria by cryo-fluorescence followed by CSTET (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: JC-1 damaged mitochondrial ultrastructure and disrupted granules, likely by perturbing the potential it reports on.
source: However, JC-1 damaged mitochondrial ultrastructure and disrupted granules, likely by perturbing the potential it reports on.
evidence: This is observed in Figure 4 and inferred from the known mechanism of JC-1.

claim: Fluorescent sensors may perturb organelle chemistry and morphology, effects that are readily seen in CSTET.
source: This experiment demonstrated the feasibility of correlative fluorescence/CSTET studies but also emphasizes that fluorescent sensors may perturb organelle chemistry and morphology, effects that are readily seen in CSTET.
evidence: This is concluded from the observation of JC-1 effects on mitochondria.

claim: Intentional depolarization of mitochondria by treating cells with FCCP eliminated calcium deposits.
source: Intentional depolarization of mitochondria by treating cells with carbonyl cyanide p-[trifluoromethoxy]-phenyl-hydrazone (FCCP) eliminated calcium deposits (Figure 5A,B,C), demonstrating the relevance of the proton gradient to matrix granule formation in cells.
evidence: This is observed in Figures 5A,B,C.

claim: The elimination of calcium deposits by FCCP demonstrates the relevance of the proton gradient to matrix granule formation in cells.
source: Intentional depolarization of mitochondria by treating cells with carbonyl cyanide p-[trifluoromethoxy]-phenyl-hydrazone (FCCP) eliminated calcium deposits (Figure 5A,B,C), demonstrating the relevance of the proton gradient to matrix granule formation in cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that depolarization eliminates granules.

claim: Ion deposition is reversible.
source: As granules were found consistently in untreated non-confluent fibroblasts and thus presumably existed before FCCP treatment, this experiment also showed that ion deposition is reversible, though the rate of mobilization remains to be determined.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that granules present before treatment are eliminated by FCCP.

claim: The matrices of some FCCP-treated mitochondria showed contrast similar to cytosol, indicating depletion of soluble heavy elements as well.
source: The matrices of some FCCP-treated mitochondria showed contrast similar to cytosol, indicating depletion of soluble heavy elements as well (Figure 5A,B,C).
evidence: This is observed in Figures 5A,B,C and interpreted as indicating ion depletion.

claim: Neighboring mitochondria, including some sharing contiguous outer membranes, displayed very different matrix densities.
source: Remarkably, neighboring mitochondria, including some sharing contiguous outer membranes (Figure 5C), displayed very different matrix densities, revealing that variations in soluble ion concentrations, and not only the presence of dense deposits, can be detected by CSTET.
evidence: This is observed in Figure 5C.

claim: Variations in soluble ion concentrations, and not only the presence of dense deposits, can be detected by CSTET.
source: Remarkably, neighboring mitochondria, including some sharing contiguous outer membranes (Figure 5C), displayed very different matrix densities, revealing that variations in soluble ion concentrations, and not only the presence of dense deposits, can be detected by CSTET.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of different matrix densities in neighboring mitochondria.

claim: Granule-free mitochondria were observed in MCF10A breast epithelial cells that were undergoing a burst of proliferation at the time of vitrification.
source: In one instance, we observed granule-free mitochondria in MCF10A breast epithelial cells that were undergoing a burst of proliferation at the time of vitrification (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is observed in Figure 5D.

claim: A group of mitochondria in rapidly proliferating MCF10A cells displayed the dark matrix observed in other mitochondria, suggesting that they remain polarized and have a high content of soluble calcium, but were clearly devoid of granules.
source: A group of mitochondria in this case were observed to display the dark matrix observed in BF images of other mitochondria, suggesting that they remain polarized and have a high content of soluble calcium, but they were clearly devoid of granules.
evidence: This is observed in the CSTET data and interpreted based on the matrix appearance.

claim: Sequestration and mobilization of calcium occurs according to local signaling and energetic requirements and can exhibit substantial heterogeneity within certain cell populations.
source: It therefore appears that sequestration and mobilization of calcium occurs according to local signaling and energetic requirements and can exhibit substantial heterogeneity within certain cell populations.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of heterogeneity in granule presence across different cells and conditions.

claim: WI-38 fibroblast cells grown for longer periods and allowed to reach 90% to 95% confluence on grids often contained mitochondria with few or no granules.
source: We also observed that WI-38 fibroblast cells grown for longer periods and allowed to reach 90% to 95% confluence on grids often contained mitochondria with few or no granules (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is observed in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Confluent fibroblasts are highly metabolically active, using substantial energy to produce and secrete large amounts of extracellular matrix precursors.
source: Notably, confluent fibroblasts are highly metabolically active, using substantial energy to produce and secrete large amounts of extracellular matrix precursors (Lemons et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Calcium uptake by mitochondria may take precedence over ATP synthesis.
source: By contrast, the observation that calcium uptake by mitochondria may take precedence over ATP synthesis (Bernardi, 1999) is not widely appreciated.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Formation of solid calcium phosphate complexes in mitochondria has been described in the context of bone formation.
source: Formation of solid calcium phosphate complexes in mitochondria has been described in the context of bone formation (Boonrungsiman et al., 2012; Sutfin et al., 1971; Kerschnitzki et al., 2016), but our study points to broader purposes for mitochondrial granules, beyond calcification.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Mitochondrial granules have broader purposes beyond calcification.
source: Formation of solid calcium phosphate complexes in mitochondria has been described in the context of bone formation (Boonrungsiman et al., 2012; Sutfin et al., 1971; Kerschnitzki et al., 2016), but our study points to broader purposes for mitochondrial granules, beyond calcification.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of granules in non-mineralizing cells.

claim: Solid-state storage must be considered in a general accounting of cellular calcium, even for non-mineralizing cells.
source: CSTET visualization of calcium sequestration in a variety of unfixed and unstained whole cells strengthens the notion that solid-state storage must be considered in a general accounting of cellular calcium, even for non-mineralizing cells.
evidence: This is concluded from the observation of granules across multiple non-mineralizing cell types.

claim: CSTET provides a direct and readily appreciable view of calcium deposition in intact cells.
source: This direct and readily appreciable view of calcium deposition in intact cells is valuable for re-focusing attention on the role of ion phase separation and remobilization in mitochondrial function.
evidence: This is demonstrated throughout the study by the visualization of granules in vitrified cells.

claim: CSTET can reveal organelle organization and elemental distribution in intact mammalian cells with no sample manipulation other than cryo-preservation.
source: With the remarkable ability to reveal organelle organization and elemental distribution in intact mammalian cells with no sample manipulation other than cryo-preservation, CSTET promises to be a pioneering technology for cell biology.
evidence: This is demonstrated throughout the study.

claim: Cells were vitrified 2 or 3 days after seeding onto microscopy grids, when they were well-adherent and showed evidence of proliferation but were still sub-confluent.
source: Unless otherwise noted, cells were vitrified 2 or 3 days after seeding onto microscopy grids, when they were well-adherent and showed evidence of proliferation but were still sub-confluent.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol used in the study.

claim: CSTET is well suited to provide deep views into cells up to >1 μm.
source: We note that CSTET is well suited to provide deep views (up to >1 μm) into cells (Rez et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and demonstrated by the tomograms in this study.

claim: Conventional cryo-TEM tomography requires technically challenging processing of thicker regions by cryo-microtomy or focused-ion beam milling.
source: For comparison, conventional cryo-TEM tomography is restricted to thin cell regions (preferably less than 300 nm) (Villa et al., 2013) or requires technically challenging processing of thicker regions by cryo-microtomy (Ladinsky et al., 2006) or focused-ion beam milling (Marko et al., 2007; Mahamid et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The equivalent liquid concentration of calcium phosphate based on the 20% volume estimate would be about 0.64 M, corresponding to 1.9 M calcium ions and 1.3 M phosphate ions.
source: The equivalent liquid concentration based on the 20% vol estimate would be about 0.64 M, corresponding to 1.9 M calcium ions and 1.3 M phosphate ions.
evidence: This is calculated from the density and volume measurements.

claim: These concentrations are compatible with the solubility of calcium ions (e.g. from CaCl2) in aqueous solution but exceed by a factor of ~10^4 the solubility of Ca3(PO4)2 in aqueous solution.
source: These concentrations are compatible with the solubility of calcium ions (e.g. from CaCl2) in aqueous solution but exceed by a factor of ~104 the solubility of Ca3(PO4)2 in aqueous solution.
evidence: This is inferred from known solubility properties and the calculated concentrations.

claim: Granules were observed in hundreds of mitochondria imaged in this study in multiple adherent mammalian cell types visualized under sub-confluent conditions.
source: Overall, granules were observed in hundreds of mitochondria imaged in this study in multiple adherent mammalian cell types visualized under sub-confluent conditions.
evidence: This summarizes the observations across the study.

claim: About 22 tomograms of untreated WI-38 fibroblasts that had grown 2 to 4 days on grids were collected, and all 66 mitochondria observed contained granules.
source: During the course of this study, about 22 tomograms of untreated WI-38 fibroblasts that had grown 2 to 4 days on grids were collected. Altogether 66 mitochondria were observed in reconstructions of these tomograms, and all these mitochondria contained granules.
evidence: This is a summary of the data collected in the study.

claim: 13 tomograms were collected from WI-38 fibroblasts that had grown for 6 or 7 days on grids without exchange of medium and were near confluence, showing 30 mitochondria, 15 of which contained granules.
source: In addition, 13 tomograms were collected from WI-38 fibroblasts that had grown for 6 or 7 days on grids without exchange of medium and were near confluence. Thirty mitochondria were observed in these tomograms, 15 of which contained granules.
evidence: This is a summary of the data collected in the study.

claim: Seven tomograms of wild-type MEFs yielded 33 mitochondria, all containing granules.
source: Seven tomograms of wild-type MEFs yielded 33 mitochondria, all containing granules, whereas 3 tomograms of MCU-/- MEFs showed 17 mitochondria, 7 of them lacking granules).
evidence: This is a summary of the data collected in the study.

claim: 3 tomograms of MCU-/- MEFs showed 17 mitochondria, 7 of them lacking granules.
source: Seven tomograms of wild-type MEFs yielded 33 mitochondria, all containing granules, whereas 3 tomograms of MCU-/- MEFs showed 17 mitochondria, 7 of them lacking granules).
evidence: This is a summary of the data collected in the study.
